title: Tucatinib alleviates postmenopausal osteoporosis by suppressing osteoclast differentiation via regulating the DRP1/NFATc1/CTSK signaling pathway.
authors: Liu, Xin; Liu, Shuang; Xu, Guoqiang; Chen, Wendi; Shi, Yuxuan; Wang, Guolong; Cao, Yongzhi; Lu, Gang; Ning, Yunna; Zhao, Yueran
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Tucatinib通过DRP1/NFATc1/CTSK通路抑制破骨细胞分化治疗骨质疏松，属于药物药理与骨代谢疾病研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模及AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) represents the most prevalent metabolic bone disease among postmenopausal women worldwide. Cathepsin K (CTSK), a key mediator of osteoclastic bone resorption, serves as a critical therapeutic target for PMOP. Through structure-based virtual screening coupled with functional validation, we identified Tucatinib as a potent CTSK inhibitor. Microscale thermophoresis (MST), molecular docking, and CTSK activity assays confirmed that Tucatinib directly binds to and inhibits CTSK, effectively suppressing osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Notably, Tucatinib attenuated NFATc1-driven osteoclast differentiation in bone marrow-derived monocytes/macrophages (BMMs). In ovariectomized mouse models, Tucatinib significantly prevented estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss. Mechanistic investigations revealed that Tucatinib maintains mitochondrial homeostasis by inhibiting dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1) phosphorylation at Ser616 during early-stage osteoclast differentiation and reducing mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) production, thereby stabilizing mitochondrial fission/fusion dynamics and suppressing NFATc1 activation. Our findings demonstrate that Tucatinib alleviates osteoporotic bone loss by simultaneously modulating the DRP1/NFATc1 axis and CTSK enzymatic activity, offering a promising dual-action therapeutic strategy for PMOP.
abstract_zh: 绝经后骨质疏松症（PMOP）是全球绝经后女性中最常见的代谢性骨病。组织蛋白酶K（CTSK）是破骨细胞骨吸收的关键介质，也是PMOP的重要治疗靶点。通过基于结构的虚拟筛选结合功能验证，我们鉴定出Tucatinib为一种有效的CTSK抑制剂。微量热泳动（MST）、分子对接和CTSK活性测定证实，Tucatinib直接结合并抑制CTSK，有效抑制破骨细胞介导的骨吸收。值得注意的是，Tucatinib减弱了骨髓来源单核细胞/巨噬细胞（BMMs）中NFATc1驱动的破骨细胞分化。在去卵巢小鼠模型中，Tucatinib显著预防了雌激素缺乏诱导的骨丢失。机制研究表明，Tucatinib通过抑制早期破骨细胞分化中动力相关蛋白1（DRP1）在Ser616位点的磷酸化，并减少线粒体活性氧（mtROS）产生，从而维持线粒体稳态，稳定线粒体分裂/融合动态，并抑制NFATc1激活。我们的研究结果表明，Tucatinib通过同时调节DRP1/NFATc1轴和CTSK酶活性来缓解骨质疏松性骨丢失，为PMOP提供了一种有前景的双重作用治疗策略。
